—
Haavard Rue
Helpdesk
he...@r-inla.org

On 26 Sep 2023 at 19:01 +0200, Tim Meehan <tme...@gmail.com>, wrote:
Hi all,

On Windows, I am running complicated models with INLA and inlabru without trouble. But when I try to do something simple with a small dataset, it crashes. Are you able to reproduce this?

df <- data.frame(y=runif(20, 50000, 100000),
                 x=2001:2020,
                 z=rep(c(0,1), 10))
lm(y ~ x * z, data=df)
bru(y ~ x * z, data=df)
inla(y ~ x * z, data=df,
     verbose=TRUE,debug=TRUE,safe=FALSE)

Any ideas? Besides dumping Windows?

Thanks! 
Tim

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Complex models work - simple models crash
parts:
For the bru version of the last test, you need a component construction; not sure which one though, but it seems you want the interactions between x and z? Then use
y ~ myeffects(~x*z, model=“fixed”)

To set initial values in inlabru for latent variables, use options=list(bru_initial=list(myeffects=c(…)))
Finn

On 26 Sep 2023, at 18:28, Tim Meehan <tme...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Thanks, Haavard! I changed the x and y values and now it works with inla(). 
But not bru(). Maybe Finn will see this. BTW, am I able to set initial values 
with one of the control.x=list() arguments to inla()? I'll dig into the help.

                 x=-10:9,

z=rep(c(0,1), 10))

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Complex models work - simple models crash
parts:
On Tuesday, September 26, 2023 at 11:45:01 AM UTC-6 Finn Lindgren wrote:
For the bru version of the last test, you need a component construction; not sure which one though, but it seems you want the interactions between x and z? Then use
y ~ myeffects(~x*z, model=“fixed”)

To set initial values in inlabru for latent variables, use options=list(bru_initial=list(myeffects=c(…)))
Finn

On 26 Sep 2023, at 18:28, Tim Meehan <tme...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Thanks, Haavard! I changed the x and y values and now it works with inla(). 
But not bru(). Maybe Finn will see this. BTW, am I able to set initial values 
with one of the control.x=list() arguments to inla()? I'll dig into the help.

df <- data.frame(y=runif(20),
                 x=-10:9,

                 z=rep(c(0,1), 10))
lm(y ~ x * z, data=df)
inla(y ~ x * z, data=df,
     verbose=TRUE, debug=TRUE, safe=FALSE)
bru(y ~ x * z, data=df)

> bru(y ~ x * z, data=df)
Error: non-conformable matrix dimensions in dimCheck(e1, e2)
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In x:z : numerical expression has 20 elements: only the first used
2: In x:z : numerical expression has 20 elements: only the first used
3: In x:z : numerical expression has 20 elements: only the first used
4: In x:z : numerical expression has 20 elements: only the first used
5: In x:z : numerical expression has 20 elements: only the first used
6: In x:z : numerical expression has 20 elements: only the first used

On Tuesday, September 26, 2023 at 11:09:38 AM UTC-6 INLA help wrote:
I guess it’s because of highly noncentered covariates that make otherwise decent initial values looks bad 

—
Haavard Rue
Helpdesk
he...@r-inla.org

On 26 Sep 2023 at 19:01 +0200, Tim Meehan <tme...@gmail.com>, wrote:
Hi all,

On Windows, I am running complicated models with INLA and inlabru without trouble. But when I try to do something simple with a small dataset, it crashes. Are you able to reproduce this?

df <- data.frame(y=runif(20, 50000, 100000),
                 x=2001:2020,
                 z=rep(c(0,1), 10))
lm(y ~ x * z, data=df)
bru(y ~ x * z, data=df)
inla(y ~ x * z, data=df,
     verbose=TRUE,debug=TRUE,safe=FALSE)

Any ideas? Besides dumping Windows?

Thanks! 
Tim
